thread:
maya: Heads-up — terraform apply for gpupool-new-eu in the canary account failed during the plan step. It errored out with a provider/plugin mismatch and zone quota allocation error. Pasting the truncated output below.

maya: ```
Error: Failed to install provider
╷
│ Error: no suitable version installed for provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/google
│ 	required: >= 4.0, < 5.0
│ 	installed: 3.85.0

Error: creating compute instance: quotaExceeded
```

aj: I saw the same in staging-canary-2 earlier. Looks like the gpupool module bumped to v2.4.0 — it added zone_affinity and changed the autoscaler IAM attachments.

sophia: Noted — v2.4.0 also introduced an optional kms block that assumes the kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter role on the service account. We haven't granted that role in the canary IAM policy.

eli: Argo reported the terraform-plan step as FAILED and left the app in a PlanHold state. Deploy-bot emitted `pipeline:tf-plan:failed`.

maya: Short-term mitigation proposal: pin gpupool module to the previous patch (v2.3.7) via a lockfile/registry pin and revert the canary branch change, then re-run plan. Long-term we need stricter module versioning and a rollout checklist.

tom: Agreed on pinning. Also suggest adding a "plan-hold" annotation in the gitops pipeline so workloads don't auto-apply module bumps until manual QA. We should avoid `terraform apply -target` in prod; prefer controlled canary cluster apply.

sophia: Architecturally, the module change is reasonable, but it's not backward compatible for clusters that don't have KMS roles. We should either make the kms block optional with explicit null/default or add a compatibility shim in the module.

aj: Short-term steps I can take: revert the module bump in the canary branch, run `terraform init -reconfigure` after clearing the plugin cache, then re-run plan against the canary cluster. If quota is the real issue we'll see it separately.

maya: I'll open a PR to pin gpupool -> v2.3.7, add a changelog entry, and include a test that runs `terraform plan` against the canary workspace. PR will include notes about IAM/KMS expectations.

tom: Can we also add a CI check that prevents module version bumps without a migration note? E.g., fail the PR if a module version is changed and no `migration.md` is added.

eli: FYI the CI logs show the client plugins were from an old cache. Command that reproduced locally: `TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/tfcache terraform init -upgrade` printed plugin mismatch. Clearing the cache fixed the init for me. We should add cache purge step in the pipeline when we change provider constraints.

sophia: We also need a runbook for state migration in case the module renames resources. Include example commands in the runbook: `terraform state mv module.gpu_pool.google_compute_instance.old_name module.gpu_pool.google_compute_instance.new_name` and `terraform import module.gpu_pool.google_kms_key.key projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/...`.

maya: Action items I captured: 1) PR to pin gpupool to v2.3.7 (I will open), 2) add plan-only canary job and manual approval gate in gitops, 3) add tf-provider-lockfile and CI check for module bumps, 4) author a state-migration runbook with import/mv examples, 5) re-run canary plan after IAM role adjustments if needed.

deploy-bot: Started CI run for PR #342 that pins gpupool -> v2.3.7. Build link: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/342/checks

aj: I'll pick up the canary apply tomorrow at 09:00 UTC and monitor quota/iam errors.

maya: Thanks. If anyone finds the root cause leaning more towards region zonal quotas instead of provider/plugin, ping me immediately so we can escalate to cloud quota team.

sophia: +1 on the runbook, happy to help write the KMS-section.

maya: I'll follow up with the PR link and checklist in ~30m. Thanks all.
